title: Legislative districts of Lanao del Sur
wikitext:
{{Short description|Legislative district of the Philippines}} {{Politics of the Philippines}} The '''legislative districts of Lanao del Sur''' are the representations of the [[Provinces of the Philippines|province]] of [[Lanao del Sur]] in the [[List of legislatures of the Philippines|various national legislatures]] of the [[Philippines]]. The province is currently represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|lower house]] of the [[Congress of the Philippines]] through its [[#1st District|first]] and [[#2nd District|second]] congressional districts. == History == {{further|Legislative district of Mindanao and Sulu|Legislative district of Lanao}} Prior to gaining separate representation, areas now under the jurisdiction of Lanao del Sur were represented under the [[Department of Mindanao and Sulu]] (1917–1935) and the historical [[Lanao (province)|Lanao Province]] (1935–1961). The enactment of Republic Act No. 2228 on May 22, 1959 divided the old Lanao Province into [[Lanao del Norte]] and [[Lanao del Sur]], and provided them each with a congressional representative.{{cite web|author=Congress of the Philippines|title=Republic Act No. 2228 - An Act to Create the Provinces of Lanao del Norte and Lanao del Sur|url=http://laws.chanrobles.com/republicacts/22_republicacts.php?id=2231|website=Chan Robles Virtual Law Library|access-date=February 18, 2017|date=May 22, 1959}} In accordance with Section 8 of R.A. 2228, the incumbent representative of Lanao Province, Laurentino Badelles, also represented Lanao del Sur until voters of the new province elected their [[Legislative districts of Lanao del Sur#Lone District (defunct)|separate representative]] in the next general election, which took place in [[1961 Philippine House of Representatives elections|1961]]. The chartered city of [[Dansalan]] (renamed to [[Marawi]] in 1956{{cite web|url=http://laws.chanrobles.com/republicacts/16_republicacts.php?id=1554|date=June 16, 1956|author=Congress of the Philippines|website=Chan Robles Virtual Law Library|access-date=February 18, 2017|title=Republic Act No. 1552 - An Act to Amend the Charter of the City of Dansalan so as to Change Its name to Marawi and Make Elective Its Mayor, Vice-Mayor and Councilors, and for other purposes}}), despite being enumerated as part of the territory of neither successor province, was designated as Lanao del Sur's seat of provincial government and became part of its [[#Lone District (defunct)|lone congressional district]]. Lanao del Sur was represented in the [[Interim Batasang Pambansa]] as part of [[Interim Batasang Pambansa#Regional Representatives|Region XII]] from 1978 to 1984, and returned [[#At-Large (defunct)|two representatives, elected at large]], to the [[Regular Batasang Pambansa]] in [[1984 Philippine parliamentary election|1984]]. Under the new Constitution which was proclaimed on February 11, 1987, the province was reapportioned into two congressional districts;{{cite web|title=1987 Constitution of the Philippines - Apportionment Ordinance|website=Official Gazette of the Republic of the Philippines|url=http://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines-ordinance/|author=1986 Constitutional Commission|date=February 2, 1987|access-date=November 19, 2017}} each elected its member to the restored [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|House of Representatives]] starting [[1987 Philippine legislative election|that same year]]. == 1st District == *'''[[Cities of the Philippines|City]]''': [[Marawi]] *'''[[Municipalities of the Philippines|Municipalities]]''': [[Bumbaran|Amai Manabilang]] (Bumbaran), [[Buadiposo-Buntong]], [[Bubong, Lanao del Sur|Bubong]], [[Ditsaan-Ramain]], [[Kapai, Lanao del Sur|Kapai]], [[Lumba-Bayabao]], [[Maguing]], [[Marantao]], [[Masiu]], [[Mulondo, Lanao del Sur|Mulondo]], [[Piagapo]], [[Poona Bayabao]], [[Saguiaran]], [[Tagoloan II]], [[Tamparan]], [[Taraka, Lanao del Sur|Taraka]], [[Wao, Lanao del Sur|Wao]] *'''Population (2020)''': 686,512{{cite web|url=https://psa.gov.ph/sites/default/files/attachments/hsd/pressrelease/2015_Table%201_Legislative%20Districts.xlsx|website=Philippine Statistics Authority|date=2015|title=Population of Population of Legislative Districts by Region, Province, and Selected Highly Urbanized/Component City: 2015|access-date=November 22, 2017}} {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center; width:40%;" |- ! width="40%"| Period !
